## Guided Tutorial 3.2: Tracing a Sale from Sales Order to General Ledger

**Context and objective.** In this tutorial, you will follow one real Charles River sale through the workbook, from the sales order to the general ledger and the cash receipt that paid for it. The goal is to practice using keys to move between tables and to see how the source-document trace connects operational data to the posted ledger. You will work with invoice SI-2025-007947, which billed a customer for two desks. Its revenue posting is the ledger row you saw in @fig-01-06, and this tutorial follows the rest of the sale.

**Prerequisites.** You need Microsoft Excel installed on your computer and the CharlesRiver.xlsx file, together with the O2C ER diagram (@fig-03-07) and the Accounting Core ER diagram (@fig-03-09). Several worksheets are large, so use filters (Data > Filter) rather than scrolling to find the rows you need.

**Step-by-step instructions.**

**Step 1.** Click on the SalesInvoice worksheet and filter the InvoiceNumber column for SI-2025-007947. Record the SalesInvoiceID (7947), the SalesOrderID (1697), the CustomerID (135), and the amounts. The invoice has a SubTotal of $688.42, a FreightAmount of $51.00, and a TaxAmount of $48.06, for a GrandTotal of $787.48.

**Step 2.** Click on the SalesInvoiceLine worksheet and filter the SalesInvoiceID column for 7947. The invoice has one line (SalesInvoiceLineID 10645) for 2 units at a UnitPrice of $344.21, a LineTotal of $688.42. The line carries three foreign keys that lead back into the O2C group: ItemID 218, SalesOrderLineID 6522, and ShipmentLineID 10449.

**Step 3.** Follow the foreign keys. In the ShipmentLine worksheet, filter ShipmentLineID for 10449: it belongs to ShipmentID 3603 and records 2 units shipped. In the Shipment worksheet, ShipmentID 3603 is shipment SH-2025-003603, shipped on 2025-03-02, three days before the invoice date. In the SalesOrderLine worksheet, SalesOrderLineID 6522 belongs to SalesOrderID 1697. In the SalesOrder worksheet, that is order SO-2024-001697, placed on 2024-11-21 by CustomerID 135, and the Customer worksheet shows that customer 135 is Sullivan-Mcdonald, a wholesale customer. In the Item worksheet, ItemID 218 is FUR-DSK-0075, an Alder Desk in the Furniture group. Notice that the order line covers a larger quantity than this invoice: the order was shipped and invoiced in several parts, and this invoice bills only the 2 units shipped on SH-2025-003603.

**Step 4.** Now cross into the Accounting Core. Click on the GLEntry worksheet and filter SourceDocumentType for SalesInvoice and SourceDocumentID for 7947. You should see four rows, all posted on 2025-03-05: a debit to account 1020 of $787.48, and credits to account 4010 of $688.42, account 4050 of $51.00, and account 2050 of $48.06. Total the Debit and Credit columns for these rows and confirm that the entry balances. Notice that only the revenue row has a SourceLineID (10645), because it is the only posting that comes from a specific invoice line.

**Step 5.** Look up each AccountID from Step 4 in the Account worksheet. Account 1020 is Accounts Receivable (an asset), 4010 is Sales Revenue - Furniture and 4050 is Freight Revenue (both revenue), and 2050 is Sales Tax Payable (a liability). Compare account 4010 with the RevenueAccountID of item 218 in the Item worksheet: the item's account mapping is what directed this revenue to the furniture revenue account.

**Step 6.** The same sale also created postings when the desks were shipped. In the GLEntry worksheet, filter SourceDocumentType for Shipment and SourceDocumentID for 3603. The rows with SourceLineID 10449 debit 5010 COGS - Furniture and credit 1040 Inventory - Finished Goods for $459.32 each, which is 2 units at the item's standard cost of $229.66. The shipment's remaining rows record the freight cost of delivering it.

**Step 7.** Finally, trace the payment. In the CashReceiptApplication worksheet, filter SalesInvoiceID for 7947. One application (CashReceiptApplicationID 10686) applies $787.48 from CashReceiptID 3043 on 2025-04-17. In the CashReceipt worksheet, receipt 3043 is CR-2025-003043, a check for $23,870.99. Filter the CashReceiptApplication worksheet for CashReceiptID 3043 and you will see that this single check paid seven invoices, which is why a junction table is needed. In GLEntry, the receipt itself (SourceDocumentType CashReceipt, SourceDocumentID 3043) debits Cash and Cash Equivalents and credits 2060 Customer Deposits and Unapplied Cash, and the application (SourceDocumentType CashReceiptApplication, SourceDocumentID 10686) moves $787.48 from account 2060 to settle Accounts Receivable.

@fig-03-10 summarizes the path you have just followed.

![Annotated Charles River Cross-Group Traced Path.](/visuals/svg/fig-03-10-cross-group-traced-path.svg){#fig-03-10 fig-alt="A step-by-step trace of invoice SI-2025-007947. Steps 1 to 4 follow sales order SO-2024-001697 for customer 135, Sullivan-Mcdonald, through sales order line 6522 (item FUR-DSK-0075, Alder Desk), shipment line 10449 on shipment SH-2025-003603, and invoice line 10645 (2 units at $344.21). Step 5 shows the invoice's four GLEntry rows found through SourceDocumentType SalesInvoice and SourceDocumentID 7947: Dr Accounts Receivable $787.48, Cr Sales Revenue - Furniture $688.42, Cr Freight Revenue $51.00, and Cr Sales Tax Payable $48.06. Step 6 classifies account 4010 as revenue. Side panels show the shipment's COGS and inventory postings of $459.32 and the cash application of $787.48 from receipt CR-2025-003043."}

**Checkpoint.** You should now be able to explain how a sale flows from the O2C group into the Accounting Core. You should be able to show that the invoice's ledger postings balance and that the debit to Accounts Receivable equals the invoice's GrandTotal of $787.48. You should be able to identify SourceDocumentType and SourceDocumentID as the columns that trace a GLEntry row back to its source document, and explain why the same sale produces postings from three different documents: the shipment, the invoice, and the cash application. If you can explain all of these points, you have the cross-group navigation skills that the remaining chapters require.
